compiled.why: The question first selects customers by a condition on the calls (those served by agent 9143e7f7-...), then counts, for each other agent, how many of those customers they also handled. That needs a self-join of fct_calls on customer, or a subquery of the customers chosen by that agent. A filter on the agent's own calls would drop the other agents' calls, so this can't be expressed as a single measure, dimensions and filters over one fact table.

WITH tulsa_callers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_key
  FROM `fennmoor-dw.dw_contact_center.fct_calls`
  WHERE queue_name = 'Tulsa Contact Center'
    AND customer_key IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  h.product_line,
  COUNT(DISTINCT h.customer_key) AS customers
FROM tulsa_callers t
JOIN `fennmoor-dw.dw_core.dim_customer` c
  ON c.customer_key = t.customer_key
JOIN `fennmoor-dw.dw_customer.customer_product_holdings` h
  ON h.customer_key = c.customer_key
WHERE h.open_accounts > 0
GROUP BY h.product_line
ORDER BY customers DESC

compiled.why: The question asks for customers who satisfy two conditions in two different fact tables: they have a card purchase at merchant MID000100000 and also a closure call in the contact center. That is an existence-in-another-fact restriction (customers with a row in one fact, counted from the other), which this request form cannot express. The count would have to be over the customers found in both tables, and the request can only aggregate each fact on its own and join the results by dimension, so it cannot intersect the two sets of customers.
